answer: The flow front is marked with pegs and surveyed every week, and the survey book holds a position for each peg the team has set. A river peg hammered in by a stranger fails the survey: at the thread of the front the pegs must march exactly as the lava advanced, and a strange peg sits where no lava flowed. Forging a season of surveys means hiring a surveyor, walking hot ground for months and paying 18,900, and the jetty entry in the survey book is checked against the flow's own map, so a peg whose position was never surveyed is pulled up.
